about.title: About this project
about.whatThisIsText: A SMILES string is parsed with RDKit into molecular descriptors and fingerprints, then scored by calibrated machine-learning models across 16 ADMET tasks — solubility, blood-brain barrier penetration, a 12-assay Tox21 toxicity panel, clinical trial toxicity, and FDA approval likelihood — each with an accompanying confidence estimate.
about.datasetsSourceNote: All four datasets are aggregated via MoleculeNet. See data/README.md in the project repository for exact sizes and licensing.
about.confidenceText: Confidence is not the model's overall accuracy — it is an estimate of how reliable this particular prediction is, derived from probability calibration (Platt/isotonic scaling). A confidence of 70% means the calibrated probability for this molecule should be trusted about as much as similar 70%-confidence predictions have historically been correct — it is not a guarantee about this individual molecule.
about.applicabilityDomainText: The applicability-domain flag is a heuristic distance check against the training data's descriptor space, not a guarantee: an "in-domain" molecule can still be mispredicted, and an "out-of-domain" one is simply a stronger signal to treat the result with caution.

limitations.overfitting: Documented train-vs-validation overfitting on 13 of the 16 tasks (all 12 Tox21 assays except NR-AhR, plus clinical trial toxicity) — train-set performance is dramatically better than validation, so the reported validation/test metrics (not the train metrics) are the honest estimate of real-world performance.
limitations.perTaskModels: Per-task models, not a true multi-task architecture — each task's winning model is trained independently, so cross-task consistency is not guaranteed.
limitations.calibration: Confidence is a proxy derived from the calibrated probability's distance from 0.5, not a separately validated uncertainty measure for every task.
limitations.datasetOverlap: The four source datasets barely overlap by molecule — most training examples for any one task come from a single source dataset, so cross-task generalization should not be assumed.
limitations.tox21Coverage: The Tox21 panel covers 12 specific assay mechanisms; it does not represent an exhaustive test of toxicity and should not be read as a complete safety profile.
limitations.applicabilityDomainHeuristic: The applicability-domain flag is a descriptor-distance heuristic, not a formal guarantee of prediction reliability.

about.disclaimerText: Research/educational use only. Not for clinical or regulatory decision-making. Predictions include explicit confidence and applicability-domain indicators and must never be treated as medical, regulatory, or safety guidance.
